page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-64 is a high-memory compute instance based on the x86_64 architecture. The virtual machine is powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon processor equipped with 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. It features 512 GB of total system RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio designed for memory-intensive computing. Cache allocations include 32 KB L1 data, 1.0 MB L2, and 33 MB L3 cache, with hardware instructions including AVX-512 and AES. The server does not bundle local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs, requiring external storage resources for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations reflect high capability in specialized parallel and vector-heavy execution. The instance scores in the top 25 percent for Clang software compilation at 40780.0 and PassMark CPU extended instructions at 51784.29. General multi-core throughput and memory operations place within the median 50 percent, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 60212.33, large-block read memory bandwidth of 162.21 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput reaching 53.97 million operations per second. However, without discrete accelerator hardware, large language model generation on 70B parameter models performs in the lower quartile at 2.56 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-64 offers dense memory capacity per core, eliminating the need to over-provision CPU resources solely to obtain significant RAM. The architecture trades local storage and GPU support for memory density and multi-core stability. This hardware configuration is appropriate for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis key-value stores, memory-bound caching tiers, extensive continuous integration builds, and complex data extraction, transformation, and loading pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-64 is a memory-oriented server type configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 2.8 GHz processor. It delivers 512 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Performance profiles show strong capability in vector processing and multi-threaded compilation, evidenced by upper-quartile scores in PassMark extended instructions and Geekbench Clang build tests. Core system throughput aligns with median performance tiers, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core result of 60212.33 and Redis throughput of 53.97 million operations per second. While unsuited for large parameter LLM text generation due to the absence of dedicated accelerators, its memory density provides an efficient architecture for memory-bound workloads, such as enterprise in-memory databases, caching clusters, and extensive CI/CD build environments.
